title: Prescriber-requested Schedule II partial fill: when the per-fill specification is owed and what the pharmacy records
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(3), where a practitioner issues a prescription for a Schedule II controlled substance and wants the prescription to be partially filled, the practitioner must specify the quantity to be dispensed in each partial filling on the face of the written prescription, in the written record of the emergency oral prescription, or in the record for an electronic prescription. That information, except an authorization for partial filling at a later date, must be included on the prescription, with the other information 21 CFR 1306.05 requires, at the time the practitioner signs it, or, for an emergency oral prescription, communicated by the prescribing practitioner to the pharmacist during the oral communication. After consultation with a pharmacist, a practitioner may authorize a partial fill at a date after the prescription was initially issued, but the prescription must be filled not later than 30 days after the date on which it is written, except that the remaining portions of a partially filled emergency oral prescription, if filled, must be filled not later than 72 hours after it is issued. Under 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(5)(i), upon partially filling a prescription at the request of the prescribing practitioner, as requested when the prescriber issued the prescription, the pharmacist must make a notation of the quantity dispensed on the face of the written prescription or in the pharmacy's electronic records, in the written record or the pharmacy's electronic records of the emergency oral prescription, or in the record of the electronic prescription. When the pharmacist partially fills a prescription after the prescriber has conveyed the request in a consultation with a pharmacist, the pharmacist must note 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill', the name of the practitioner, the date and time of the discussion, and the pharmacist's initials. For each such partial filling, whether requested by the prescriber on the prescription or after consultation with the pharmacist, the pharmacy must maintain a record of dispensing that includes the date of each dispensing, the name or initials of the individual who dispensed the substance, and all other information 21 CFR 1306.22(c) requires for Schedule III and IV prescription refills; for electronic prescriptions, the quantity dispensed, the date dispensed and the dispenser must be linked to each electronic controlled substance prescription record.
exam_relevance: Tests that the practitioner's per-fill specification is owed only when the practitioner wants the prescription partially filled, and what the pharmacist records when the prescriber asked on the prescription rather than in a later consultation, as distinct from the patient-side notation in 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(5)(ii).

authority.name: Partial filling at the request of the prescribing practitioner, and how the pharmacy records it

numeric_facts.fact: Latest fill after a practitioner authorizes a later partial fill in consultation with a pharmacist
numeric_facts.unit: days after the date the prescription is written
numeric_facts.conditions: Except that the remaining portions of a partially filled emergency oral prescription, if filled, must be filled not later than 72 hours after it is issued

exceptions: The per-fill specification is owed only where the practitioner wants the prescription partially filled; a request by the patient, a minor patient's parent or legal guardian, or an adult patient's caregiver named in a medical power of attorney is made under 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(4) and does not depend on it.

The 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill' notation belongs to a partial fill the prescriber authorized in a later consultation with a pharmacist, not to one specified on the prescription when it was issued.
common_confusions: Treating the practitioner's per-fill specification as a precondition of every request-based Schedule II partial fill.
Recording a requester and a request date for a partial fill the prescriber specified on the prescription, where 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(5)(i) calls for a notation of the quantity dispensed.
Omitting the record of dispensing, which the pharmacy keeps for every prescriber-requested partial filling whether the request was on the prescription or made in consultation.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.13(b)(3) and (b)(5)(i) read on 2026-09-11 in the current eCFR section page (shown as up to date as of 9/09/2026) and in the eCFR versioner text of 21 CFR part 1306 as of 2026-09-08. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
